[title] Result: 2.4x more requests per second
[body] Same hardware: 8 GPUs, same latency target
[body] Median response time unchanged
[body] Measured on a real chat workload

novice.takeaway: The new method achieved 2.4x more requests per second on the same hardware without slowing down response times, tested on real chat data.
questions: What counts as a 'real chat workload'?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe their method significantly improves efficiency without sacrificing speed.

peer.takeaway: The presented method achieves 2.4x higher request throughput on the same hardware without increasing median latency, validated on a real chat workload.
questions: What exactly is the 'latency target' threshold used?
How was 'real chat workload' generated or sourced?
Does 2.4x match the earlier p99 goodput claim exactly?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their system doubles-plus throughput at no latency cost.

expert.takeaway: On the same 8-GPU setup with fixed latency target, the system achieves 2.4x higher requests/sec with unchanged median latency on a real chat workload.
questions: Is this p99 goodput or raw throughput, per slide 1's claim?
What request rate/concurrency defines 'more requests per second'?
How does median-only reporting align with earlier p99 latency focus?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to believe the combined techniques deliver a validated 2.4x throughput gain without latency regression.
